brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut to ₹0.65–0.80/pc on higher-volume caps, backed by market-fair pricing and five credible alternates ready to quote.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price reduction to ₹0.65–0.80/pc on our main cap SKUs at higher committed volumes.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc for typical induction-wad PP caps, down from current market band of ₹0.85–0.95/pc
priceAsk.basis: Open-market asking prices for 28 mm induction-wad PP cap sit at ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The market verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — so there is room to move lower if we lock in volume or relax tolerances.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 Days After Receipt — no reason to extend.

brief.financialLeverage: Empire Industries publishes no financials, so we can't see their profit, debt, or how tight cash is for them. That means we build our case on what we do know: the open market shows room to negotiate down to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume, and we have five strong alternates — including India's largest rigid-packaging converter, Manjushree Technopack (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B) — ready to qualify. Without their numbers, we lean on competition and our own data: we spend ₹67.47 L/year with them, enough to matter, and if they won't move we can shift share to a second source.

evidence.point: Market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap runs ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec.
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: We spend ₹67.47 L a year with them on rigid plastic packaging — enough volume to command a better rate.
HDPE resin import unit value stands at 87.61 ₹/kg — raw-material visibility to cross-check any cost claims.
Manjushree Technopack, India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue and health score B (65/100), is a top second-source candidate for pharma bottles and caps.
Mold-Tek Packaging, a listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100), offers strong, profitable capacity as a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate with proven scale.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma packaging; strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging specialist (₹701.17 Cr revenue, health C 51/100) — broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Empire Industries publishes no financials, so we can't gauge their cash position or stability — if they're struggling, a hard push could backfire; watch for any signs of delivery trouble.
Our ₹67.47 L annual spend may be small to them if they're a large group — confirm our share of their capacity before assuming we have strong leverage.

Market backups (Reliance Industries, Srichakra Polyplast, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia Polypro, Ganesha Ecosphere, Chemco Plastic) are leads to qualify (verify before RFQ) — not yet priced or audited, so don't rely on them in the first meeting.
If we squeeze too hard without a second source fully qualified, we risk a supply gap — run a parallel RFQ to Manjushree and Mold-Tek now to have a live fallback.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're seeing open-market cap prices with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume, and we're qualifying Manjushree and Mold-Tek as second sources — let's talk about how you can match that and keep our business.
